Order 
With the consent of parties, the matter is finally heard at motion stage.

2. This appeal preferred by Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arises out of award dated 12/5/2023 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sheopur in Claim Case No. 35/2021; whereby, respondents No. 1 to 3/claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs. 10,05,000/- alongwith interest for the death of Mukesh Panchal in road accident dated 13/5/2020 and liability of payment of compensation amount was fastened over Insurance Company primarily.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC vide I.A.No. 6137/2024 to submit that on the date of accident, offending vehicle was not insured with appellant Insurance Company and instead it was insured with Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15660 2 MA-8202-2023 filed documents in that relation.

He submits the Claims Tribunal erred in fastening Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs Pappi Bai on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100584974/
1 the liability of payment of compensation amount over the Insurance Company and thus and for just decision of the matter, these documents are necessary.

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that if I.A with respect to above is allowed, then,
matter will have to be remitted back to Tribunal to decide the matter afresh.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that if I.A. filed by appellant is allowed, then, matter be remitted back so that they could also adduce evidence in rebuttal, if any.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. At appellate stage, learned counsel for the appellant filed such documents under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC and prayed to take on record these documents so that actual facts could be brought on record and also submitted that why such documents could not be brought before the Claims Tribunal.

8. In view of above, in this Court's opinion, document filed by appellants along with I.A. are necessary and relevant for just decision of the case and appellant has stated reasons for not filing the same before the trial Court.

9. In view of above, I.A.No. 6137/2024 filed by appellant is allowed and documents filed along with the I.A are taken on record and the impugned award NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15660 3 MA-8202-2023 is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the Claims Tribunal for limited purpose of taking document filed alongwith this application on record and allow parties to adduce evidence regarding with which Insurance Company, the offending vehicle was registered at the time of accident, and in rebuttal also allow opposite parties for cross-examination and evidence, if the opposite party seeks to produce and thereafter pass award afresh.
10. Let the aforesaid exercises be completed within a period of six months from the date of appearance of the parties before the Tribunal.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 14/10/2024 and thereafter, as directed by the learned Claims Tribunal.

11. The office is directed to immediately send back the record of the Claims Tribunal, if any,
alongwith the copy of this Order.

With the aforesaid observation, this miscellaneous appeal is finally disposed of.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
JAI PRAKASH SOLANKI 2024.09.13 15:30:51 +05'30'
